solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To go with hallucinogen ultimately wastes my time

parts.note: E is the usual shorthand for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letter of the word wastes

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A warning that a hallucinogenic drug does nothing but waste the speaker's time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes only the last letter of 'wastes'; 'my' is the exclamation, as in 'my goodness', not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to go along with them, so the verb is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Chemists' fundamental flaw, as atomic numbers quickly made clear

indicators.note: something hastily sorted out has had its parts put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flaw in a chemistry theory exposed quickly by atomic numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quickly made clear' signals rearranging FLAW AS ATOMIC together with NOS, the abbreviation for 'numbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: This principle, relating reaction rates to concentrations, is one of the basic laws chemists rely on, a fundamental of their subject.

clue.text: Promise given by character pursuing first of spinsters on shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
the letter that comes right after the opening one of spinsters, i.e. its second character

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A promise made by someone who follows unmarried women left on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character pursuing first of spinsters' is the letter after S in that word, i.e. P, not S itself; 'on shelf' puns on unmarried women.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn undertaking, a direct synonym for a promise.

clue.text: He's no doubt who we're talking about

definitions.meaning: someone who has no doubt is sure of things, a person who is certain
a phrase used to refer to somebody without naming them, as in 'a certain someone'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both describes a confident individual and stands in for an unnamed party under discussion.

clue.text: Support one current month breaking into the next

indicators.note: the first pieces burst into the middle of the month that follows

parts.note: May is the next month after April, taken here as the month following
a means one, as in a single thing
inst. (instant) is the old business abbreviation for this month

explanation.surface: One month bleeding into the next, offered as some kind of prop.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is commercial jargon, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.', meaning this month; 'the next' month is taken as MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief prop or support of something, originally a stay rope on a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Characteristic of saints portrayed being a little squiffy?

definitions.meaning: saints in paintings have glowing haloes, so their heads are bright with light
squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk, which brings dizziness

explanation.definitionFit: Giddiness from drink is the everyday sense; the haloed heads of painted saints give the punning literal one.

clue.text: Sort of accoutrement was successful in war and what followed broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken out over the air, so we want how the words sound

parts.words: was successful in war and what followed
parts.note: won (was successful in war) followed by peace (what comes after war)

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit, a victory in war and the settlement afterwards, all announced.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, WON PEACE gives the hyphenated garment term.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece is a garment such as a swimsuit made as a single item, so it is a kind of clothing accessory.

clue.text: Another of those at the Yard, all there on the ladder

definitions.text: Another of those at the Yard

parts.note: someone all there is mentally sound, steady and stable
a companion ladder is a ship's stairway between decks, so companion stands for it

explanation.surface: A Scotland Yard detective described as sane and climbing the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Yard' suggests Scotland Yard but is a stable yard; 'all there' is idiom for sane.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable companion is a fellow horse kept in the same yard, hence another of its occupants.

clue.text: £500 and I'll do it!

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds, and a bribe of that size suggests a shady deal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' is old London slang for £500, so the offer is literally monkey business.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business means underhand or dishonest dealing, exactly what a cash-for-favours offer is.

clue.text: Soon to be delivered from ring road flooded by a river

indicators.note: a road under floodwater is surrounded by it, so the first pieces go inside

parts.note: a means one
O is ring-shaped
R is the usual map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Delivery delayed because the ring road has been flooded by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring road' reads as one thing, a bypass, but splits into two abbreviations; 'a' is the number one, not the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods ordered but not yet received are expected shortly, so they are awaiting delivery.

clue.text: Sisters in this cabin finally put overboard!

definitions.note: the word for the condition of being a nun, used here collectively for the sisters of a convent

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of cabin

parts.note: to unship is to remove or unload from a vessel

explanation.surface: Nuns aboard a vessel, one of whose cabins has just been thrown into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this' is a link; the answer reads like NUNS + HIP but splits as N + UNSHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare noun covers nuns as a body or the state of being one, so it stands for the sisters.

clue.text: Offensive about final word by Queen on MP's disposition

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the others, so the rest is placed within it

parts.note: the Tet offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another places it after, so the Queen follows the MP
set beside the preceding pieces, the final word comes after them

parts.note: Member of Parliament, as written
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: An attack on the last word from the monarch regarding an MP's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' is a noun here, the Tet offensive of the Vietnam War, not an adjective describing rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperament is a person's nature or characteristic mood, the same as their disposition.

clue.text: Sound views from this digger?

definitions.meaning: Plymouth ... is a clifftop park overlooking Plymouth Sound, a bay on the English south coast
a long-handled garden tool for breaking soil

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is a stretch of water, not noise; Plymouth's seafront promenade gives the place-name sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden tool is used to break up earth, and a raised headland of the same name overlooks Plymouth Sound.

clue.text: Attending party? Not before time, staying in

definitions.text: Attending party? Not before time, staying in

parts.words: Attending party? Not before time, staying in
parts.note: turning up after the start yet remaining in vogue, since 'in' means trendy

explanation.walkthrough: 'staying in' looks like staying at home, but 'in' means stylish: arriving late while still being in.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at a social event deliberately behind schedule is a stylish habit, so this phrase describes a late arrival still in vogue.

clue.text: Start work, but not from home

parts.note: an engine that fires works, as in sparking into action
away means not at home

explanation.surface: Instruction to begin your job, but in an office rather than at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start work' reads as one phrase, but 'Start' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an invitation to begin, as in telling someone to go ahead with their questions.

clue.text: Doing parts eventually quite personal

indicators.note: the phrase is split apart to let the other piece in

parts.note: in time means eventually
at means engaged in, as in 'what are you at?'

explanation.surface: Taking on roles that eventually become rather personal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' is a verb here: IN TIME parts to admit AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intimate is very private and close to the person, which matches quite personal.

clue.text: Dry, this drowned valley, from the East?

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: A dry valley that has become flooded, seen from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' is a verb, to air; read from the east it turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long coastal inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley, as in Galicia.

clue.text: Press on after bum steer from woodworker

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second, which follows it
bum is slang for bad or false, so the letters are given a faulty arrangement

parts.note: to urge on is to press on, spur forward

explanation.surface: A carpenter given bad advice told to carry on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum steer' is an idiom for bad advice, but 'bum' rearranges STEER as TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist prunes and treats trees, so a playful woodworker, working on living wood.

clue.text: To swap for horse's head, take a general

indicators.note: one letter is exchanged for another in the word that follows
the front letter of the horse word is the one exchanged

parts.note: a pommel horse is the gymnastics apparatus
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A command to swap for a horse's head, then capture a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' gives POMMEL, as in pommel horse; R (recipe, 'take') replaces its head P.
explanation.definitionFit: Erwin Rommel was a German field marshal of the Second World War, the 'Desert Fox'.

clue.text: Legwear only sported in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for the Canadian province

indicators.note: sport can mean frolic or play about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stockings worn only in a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sported' looks like 'worn', fitting the legwear, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are stockings, originally made of nylon, worn on the legs.

clue.text: Painting eg Io from rear is one representation of moon!

parts.note: painting is a form of art

indicators.note: read from the back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Io is the setter, who refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A painting of Io, Jupiter's moon, seen from behind as a lunar image.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is also a moon, but here it is the setter's name: ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis, the Greek goddess, was associated with the moon and often depicted with a crescent.

clue.text: So-called imitator of human speech no linguist initially accepts

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the other, so it goes inside
initially points to the opening letter of linguist

parts.note: the mina or mynah is a bird that mimics human speech

explanation.surface: A mimic of human speech that no linguist will take seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: MINA is the mynah bird, a talking mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in name only, so it is merely called that.

clue.text: Boss, not European, going off on one

indicators.note: something going off has exploded, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager, not from the continent, losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not European' looks like an instruction to drop E, but it is all part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Carried on the body, as with keys in a pocket, is what the phrase means: on oneself.
